definition.q: pairwise disagreement of S between two same-model ratings of the same text (re-rating and repeats), every unordered pair counted once; for GLM-5.3 this is the disagreement of the adaptive thinking-then-fallback workflow as run, NOT fixed-setting variation

definition.q_fixed_primary: fixed-setting pairs whose two ratings are both primary (thinking) successes
definition.q_mixed: pairs of one thinking success and one no-thinking fallback
definition.draw_disagreement_mean: mean over covered texts of 1 - sum_v p_v^2: the probability that two independent WITH-REPLACEMENT draws from the text's pool differ, which is what the replay uses (a text with 2 ratings gives q/2 of its pairwise value, 4 ratings 3q/4)

identical_text_controls.note: identical-text pairs: a per-text replay (caching) cannot change S between them; the expected change rate under independent per-checkpoint draws is 1 - sum_v p_v^2 over the text's same-model rating distribution (exact). different-text pairs: transition class up/flat/down against the defect-corrected layer.

checkpoint_effect.definition: apparent up-transition = adjacent increase in a replayed sequence at a position where the reference sequence (per-text majority of the same-model pool; ties -> that pool's re-rating) has no increase; replay null = independent draw per checkpoint from its text's pool, texts fixed; exact enumeration
checkpoint_effect.design_note: the comparison is BETWEEN lineages of different lengths, texts, models and pool distributions, not one lineage thinned to different k; it cannot isolate a checkpoint-count effect, and the observed record contributes a single apparent-up event
checkpoint_effect.heuristic_note: 1-(1-q/2)^(k-1) assumes a constant up-probability q/2 at every adjacent pair, independent adjacent events (they share a rating) and no reference exclusion; it is a heuristic, not the probability under the replay null. Pairwise q counts each observed pair once; the replay draws with replacement, whose per-text disagreement is draw_disagreement_mean (1/2 of pairwise q with two ratings, 3/4 with four)

definitions.stability: probability that two independent runs of the procedure reach the same conclusion (sum of squared exact replay probabilities), mean over lineages fully covered by the pool; abstentions count as a value, which is why the no-rating baseline scores 1.00
definitions.detected: improvement detection: P(S_after > S_before) between the two texts of a positive pair (an abstention on either text is not a detection); expected count over the pairs whose two texts both carry at least one rating in the pool (the pilot outputs carry a GLM-5.3 and a Kimi grade, no Claude grade)
definitions.accepted: endpoint acceptance: P(S_after = 2) for the later text of a positive pair, same denominator; a constant S=2 without any rating accepts every pair, so acceptance alone is degenerate
definitions.false_change: P(S differs, both known) between the two checkpoints of a negative-control pair; identical-text pairs restricted to texts with >=2 ratings in the pool
definitions.cost: ratings per applicable lineage: k checkpoints for per-checkpoint procedures, d distinct texts for per-text procedures (x3 for majority of three)
definitions.cost_comparison: (ii) costs d <= k ratings, (iii) 3d, (iv) 3k >= 3d without caching; these are rating-count comparisons, not matched budgets: the four models' calls differ in thinking behaviour and token use, so equal rating counts are not equal compute

macros.SURVIVALTXT: Under layer~0, the four single evaluators (GLM-5.3 re-rating, Kimi~K3, Claude Opus~5 and GPT-5.6-Sol on P3/P6) and every completed same-model repeat (GLM-5.3: rep1 only, 48 P3 + 25 P6 texts, 73 repeat ratings; Claude Opus~5: three repeats of 48 P3 + 36 P6 texts, 252 repeat ratings), the improved, regressed and first-crossing conclusions are identical for 30, 29 and 27 of the 31 applicable lineages; the flips are P3 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol (final file: $S{=}2$ by GLM and Claude but $S{=}0$ by Kimi and GPT, 2-vs-2; flips improved and crossing); P3 deedy-kimi-k3 (kimi-k3-round3, t7: $S{=}1$ by Kimi, Claude and GPT but $S{=}0$ by GLM, 3-vs-1, so the rater-dependent $S{=}1$ is the majority reading; kimi-k3-round4, t14: $S{=}2$ by GLM, Kimi and Claude but $S{=}1$ by GPT, 3-vs-1; flips regressed and crossing); P6 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol (gpt-5.6-sol-main, t9 and final file: $S{=}2$ by GLM and Kimi but $S{=}1$ by Claude and GPT, 2-vs-2; flips crossing); P6 deedy-kimi-k3 (kimi-k3-round1, t21: $S{=}0$ by GLM, Claude and GPT but $S{=}1$ by Kimi, 3-vs-1; kimi-k3-round2, t7: $S{=}2$ by GLM, Kimi and Claude but $S{=}1$ by GPT, 3-vs-1; flips regressed and crossing). Among the aggregation layers, written differs from defect-corrected for two lineages (P6 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol: crossing; P6 deedy-kimi-k3: regressed, crossing) and majority of three for four lineages (P3 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol: improved, crossing; P3 deedy-kimi-k3: regressed; P6 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol: crossing; P6 deedy-kimi-k3: regressed, crossing). Under exact enumeration of the per-text replay (every distinct text's $S$ redrawn from its same-model pool; GLM-5.3 pool = the adaptive workflow as run, $q{=}0/70$ on fixed-setting and $1/3$ on mixed-mode pairs; Claude Opus~5 $q{=}0.03$), the defect-corrected improved/regressed/crossing conclusions survive with mean probability: Problem~3, 0.94/1.00/0.94 with the GLM-5.3 pool (17 of 17 covered) and 0.94/0.99/0.97 with the Claude Opus~5 pool (17 of 17 covered); Problem~6, 1.00/1.00/1.00 with the GLM-5.3 pool (9 of 12 covered) and 1.00/0.91/0.86 with the Claude Opus~5 pool (12 of 12 covered); Problem~2, no repeats by protocol.
macros.SURVIVALREFTXT: The defect-corrected reference reads improved for 12, regressed for 0 and a first crossing for 15 of the 31 lineages, so a rule that always reports ``no regression'' matches every regression conclusion, and the means hide the affected lineages, whose improved/regressed/crossing survival is below 1: with the GLM-5.3 pool, P3 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol 0.00/1.00/0.00 (final file: pool $S\in\{2\}$, reference 0); with the Claude Opus~5 pool, P3 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol 0.00/1.00/0.50 (final file: pool $S\in\{1,2\}$, reference 0), P3 deedy-kimi-k3 1.00/0.75/1.00, P6 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol 1.00/0.88/0.38, P6 deedy-kimi-k3 1.00/0.00/0.00 (kimi-k3-round2, t7: pool $S\in\{2\}$, reference 1) (a 0 means the pool never reproduces the reference conclusion, because it rates the text in parentheses the other way). Survival is agreement with an author-maintained, partly model-derived corrected reference (the written GLM$\cap$Kimi layer with 3 correction entries), not out-of-sample accuracy. The units are nested (Claude's 504 same-text pairs are six dependent pairs on each of 84 texts; lineages share problems and model families), the replay distribution is enumerated exactly from pools of two or four ratings per text, and the $B{=}1000$ Monte Carlo cross-check (maximum deviation 0.022) adds precision only, never evaluator evidence.
macros.REPLAYQTXT: Same-text disagreement on $S$: GLM-5.3, 0 of 70 fixed-setting pairs (69 thinking--thinking, 1 fallback--fallback) and 1 of 3 mixed-mode pairs (P6 p6-gpt-5.6-sol-main-t009: no-thinking fallback $S{=}2$ against thinking $S{=}1$), hence 1 of 73 for the adaptive thinking-then-fallback workflow as run; Claude Opus~5, 14 of 504 fixed-setting pairs on 84 texts ($q{=}0.03$). Completed repeats at freeze: GLM-5.3: rep1 only, 48 P3 + 25 P6 texts, 73 repeat ratings; Claude Opus~5: three repeats of 48 P3 + 36 P6 texts, 252 repeat ratings. GLM-5.3's one disagreement is a change of thinking mode, not fixed-setting stochastic variation, so every lineage covered by its pool has a deterministic pool.
macros.CHECKPOINTEFFECTTXT: In the observed record layer~0 contains 1 up-transition absent from the defect-corrected layer (1 of 31 lineages: P3 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol at final file) and 0 changes between identical adjacent texts, with no detectable association between lineage length and apparent progress (Spearman $\rho{=}0.136$, permutation $p{=}0.711$); the design compares different lineages of different lengths, texts and models, not one lineage thinned to different $k$, so it cannot isolate a checkpoint-count effect. Under the replay null (independent same-model draws per checkpoint, texts fixed; exact enumeration) the probability of at least one apparent up-transition is 0 for all 23 lineages covered by the GLM-5.3 pool (every covered text has a deterministic pool), and 0 for 24 of the 26 lineages covered by the Claude Opus~5 pool, 0.375 for P6 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol ($k{=}3$) and 0.250 for P3 deedy-kimi-k3 ($k{=}5$), a mean of 0.033 over the 19 covered lineages with $k{\ge}3$. The expression $1-(1-q/2)^{k-1}$ is only a heuristic (constant up-probability $q/2$ at every adjacent pair, independent adjacent events, no reference exclusion): with the with-replacement disagreement the replay actually draws (0.0068 for GLM-5.3, 0.0208 for Claude Opus~5; the pairwise $q$ of 0.0137 and 0.0278 counts each observed pair once) it gives 0.021 at $k{=}3$ and 0.041 at $k{=}5$ for the Claude Opus~5 pool, not the exact per-lineage values above.
macros.REMEDIESTXT: Caching one rating per distinct text costs 2.9 ratings per lineage against 3.4 for one rating per checkpoint (a rating-count comparison, not a matched budget: calls differ in thinking and token use), makes an identical-text change impossible (one rating per checkpoint: expected false-change rate 0.00 and 0.00 on the identical-text controls with the GLM-5.3 and Claude Opus~5 pools), and accepts the later text of the evaluable independently supported pairs at 7 of 7 and 3 of 3, exactly as the no-model constant-$S{=}2$ baseline does (7 of 7), because 5 of the 7 pairs are repairs of a text already at $S{=}2$ in the defect-corrected layer and test acceptance, not detection. Strict improvement detection ($S$ rises between the paired texts) is 2 of 7 and 2 of 3 with the GLM-5.3 and Claude Opus~5 pools under every rating procedure, both from P6 deedy-kimi-k3 (kimi-k3-round3, t9, $S{=}1$, to kimi-k3-main, t5 and final file, $S{=}2$), and 0 of 7 and 0 of 7 for the no-rating and constant-$S{=}2$ baselines. Majority of three per text (8.7 ratings per lineage) gives conclusion stability (improved/regressed/crossing) 1.00/1.00/1.00 and 1.00/0.99/0.96 against 1.00/1.00/1.00 and 1.00/0.98/0.96 for one rating per text, at a checkpoint abstention rate of 0\% and 0\%; the no-rating baseline is perfectly stable, detects nothing and accepts nothing, so stability is only meaningful next to detection.
macros.SAMEDEFECTTXT: On the same-defect P6 pair (turn~9 and the final file of the public GPT-default lineage, both resting on the refuted finiteness lemma; defect-corrected $S{=}1$ and 1, so the control fixes that target, not identical quality of two different texts) the Claude Opus~5 pools are $[1,1,2,1]$ and $[1,2,2,1]$: independent draws disagree with probability $1-(3/4\cdot1/2+1/4\cdot1/2)=1/2$ exactly, and because majority of three still returns $S{=}2$ for the second text with probability 1/2, it keeps the disagreement at exactly 1/2 whatever the first text's distribution (the table's identical values under every procedure are this identity, not four measurements). The GLM-5.3 pool does not cover it (turn~9: no-thinking fallback $S{=}2$ and thinking $S{=}1$; final file: no-thinking fallback $S{=}2$). The conclusion is narrow, that majority voting of this rater does not cure this error, not that repeated grading cannot supply validity: the GLM-5.3 thinking repeat rates turn~9 $S{=}1$, its notes calling the lemma false, and Claude Opus~5's ordinary grader gives both texts 2 of 7 with the false lemma as the main gap (GLM-5.3's ordinary grader: both texts 7 of 7).
macros.SOURCESTXT: repeat variability: same-text disagreement on $S$ is 0 of 70 fixed-setting pairs for GLM-5.3 (1 of 3 mixed thinking--fallback pairs, 1 of 73 for the adaptive workflow as run, on 73 texts; lower/upper fields differ on 15\%/8\% of pairs) and 14 of 504 fixed-setting pairs ($q{=}0.03$) for Claude Opus~5 on 84 texts; lower/upper fields differ on 9\%/9\% of pairs. macros.ALARMTXT: Disagreement as an alarm: the target is the credited-defective text, one with a documented defect (a correction entry, that is an independent refutation or a recorded fatal invalid step, or a public final file whose released public grade is at most 4 of 7) that at least one evaluator nevertheless rates $S{=}2$, because a text every evaluator rates $S{<}2$ is visible to an operator without any alarm. Over the 90 distinct texts of the applicable lineages (48 P3, 36 P6, 6 P2), the four single evaluators plus the GLM-5.3 repeat where present disagree on $S$ for 7 texts: all 4 credited-defective texts (P3 deedy-gpt-5.6-sol-final, P6 p6-gpt-5.6-sol-main-t009, P6 p6-kimi-k3-round2-t007 and P6 p6-deedy-gpt-5.6-sol-final; 3 distinct defects, the two P6 GPT-default texts sharing one false lemma), hence 4 of the 13 documented-defective texts, the 9 misses being never credited (P3 deedy-deepseek-v4-pro-final, deedy-gpt-5.6-sol-max-final, deedy-gpt-5.6-sol-pro-final, deedy-grok-4.5-final and deedy-muse-spark-1.1-final, public grades 1, 1, 2, 2 and 1 of 7, $S{=}0$ by every evaluator; P6 p6-deedy-deepseek-v4-pro-final, p6-deedy-gpt-5.6-sol-max-final and p6-deedy-grok-4.5-final, public grade 1 of 7 each, $S{=}0$ by every evaluator; p6-deedy-muse-spark-1.1-final, public grade 2 of 7, $S{=}1$ by every evaluator), and 3 texts without any record (P3 kimi-k3-round3-t007 and kimi-k3-round4-t014; P6 p6-kimi-k3-round1-t021).
